Characteristics:
- accuracy_class: (III) — value "III", dimensionless. Hmm, class is in recommendation.accuracy_classes too. Should I also include as characteristic? Possibly. The example schema says type_level characteristics. I can include accuracy_class value "III".

The "(per partial weighing range)" could be a note. Could record as characteristic max_number_of_scale_intervals with value {min:null, max:3000}, unit_symbol "divisions". Maybe add an additional characteristic? Or a footnote-like note. I could add scope note in description... I'll just include the value; possibly add attribute "max_scale_intervals_scope": "per partial weighing range"? Simpler: include the note as separate characteristic `max_scale_intervals_note`? Hmm. Maybe better to keep it clean: attribute `max_number_of_scale_intervals` with value {min: null, max: 3000}, unit_symbol "divisions". I might also capture "per_partial_weighing_range" as a boolean/note. I'll add a separate characteristic `scale_intervals_scope` with value "per partial weighing range". Actually, maybe not necessary. I'll skip to avoid fabrication... but it is present in the doc. I could put it in the value string? No — rules say structured. I'll add a note characteristic: `number_of_scale_intervals_scope: {value: "per partial weighing range"}`. Hmm, that's reasonable.

A list isn't specified. Options: config? It says weighing range(s): single interval or multi-interval — meaning the instrument can be single or multi-interval. This could be two "models"/configurations. But simpler: value: "Single interval / Multi-interval" as a string? Rules say lists of values that vary per model become matrix; but here it's just options available. I'll use value "Single interval, Multi-interval" or better an array? To keep parseable and within schema, I'll use a string "Single interval; Multi-interval". Hmm. Alternatively make it a list — schema says value: <number | {min, max} | string>. I'll keep string.

- power supply: multiple lines:
  - "100 – 240 V AC 50/60 Hz with external adapter" → power_supply_voltage {min:100,max:240} V; power_supply_frequency {min:50,max:60} Hz; power_supply_type "AC"; note "with external adapter"
  - "7,5 V DC to 15 V DC (supplied by an AC/DC adapter)" → decimal comma! 7,5 → 7.5. power_supply_voltage_dc: {min: 7.5, max: 15} V DC
  - "5 V DC from USB" → power_supply_voltage_usb: 5 V DC

Since there are three power supply configurations, maybe config_level? The schema has config_level for attribute × config-axis matrices. Power supply options could be config axis "power_supply_option" with conditions "external AC adapter", "AC/DC adapter", "USB". That seems apt. But it might overcomplicate. Rules example says split 110-240V AC 50/60Hz into three characteristics. Here we have three supply variants. I could emit:

type_level:
- power_supply_voltage: {min:100, max:240}, V, AC with external adapter
- power_supply_frequency: {min:50,max:60}, Hz
- power_supply_type: "AC"
- power_supply_voltage_dc: {min:7.5, max:15}, V, DC via AC/DC adapter
- power_supply_voltage_usb: 5, V, from USB

Or use config_level with axis "power_supply_option":
config_level: [
 {attribute: "power_supply_voltage", axis: "power_supply_option", values: [
   {condition: "AC external adapter", value: {min:100,max:240}, unit_symbol: "V"},

]
